summary: Backend regression + new Instant Live Tracking on IMEI Registration coverage. Added 4 new tests to /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py: (a) POST /pets with real 15-digit IMEI '860123456789012' persists lowercased and retrievable via GET /pets; (b) POST /pets without imei generates a 15-digit '860…' fallback; (c) GET /pets/{id}/history returns >=1 location point within 2.5s of pet creation (verifies _broadcast_initial_pet writes to db.locations); (d) a client on /api/ws/live receives >=1 pet_update for the new pet_id within ~1s and >=2 within ~2.5s of POST /pets. All 4 new tests pass consistently. Overall: 40/41 pass. 1 failure — test_breach_exit_then_enter_events — is a REGRESSION introduced by the new instant-broadcast feature (see rca).

minor.issue: New _broadcast_initial_pet task races with breach-detection logic. In test_breach_exit_then_enter_events the fixture creates a pet + primes it inside a 300m geofence via /api/iot/ingest; the background task then continues mutating db.pets.inside_geofence over the next ~1.6s using drifted coords. When the test's exit ingest packet arrives, prev_inside can already be False (or the background task subsequently overwrites the exit's False with True), so only 1 of the 2 expected breach events is recorded. Deterministically fails on all 3 retries (got 1 breach, expected >=2).

action_items: Fix race between _broadcast_initial_pet and breach/ingest state. Options: (1) skip inside_geofence writes in the initial broadcast (leave that to /iot/ingest and the main simulator), (2) only broadcast frames without persisting to db.pets, (3) abort the drift loop if the pet has received a real /iot/ingest since creation (compare updated_at), or (4) make the drift a no-op when the fence is small (<= some threshold).
Consider persisting `inside_geofence` on Pet model (currently defaulted via .get() only) so behavior is deterministic on fresh docs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _broadcast_initial_pet writes to db.pets AND db.locations for 4 additional frames — this synthetic data pollutes real history and can race with concurrent /iot/ingest. Consider decoupling: broadcast-only (no DB write) for the rapid frames, or gate on 'has this pet received a real ingest yet'.

First frame in _broadcast_initial_pet hardcodes inside_geofence=True regardless of the pet's geofence config — fine for a marker appearing, but semantically incorrect and can mask a pet that spawns outside its fence.

IMEI validation is server-side lenient: accepts any string, only lowercased and .strip()'d — the 15-digit numeric contract is enforced client-side only. Add a Pydantic validator (regex ^[0-9a-f]{15,16}$ or similar) so bad IMEIs are rejected at the API boundary.

asyncio.create_task result is discarded — exceptions inside _broadcast_initial_pet are only logged via the internal try/except, but a task reference should be kept (e.g., add to a set) to avoid GC of the task per Python 3.11+ recommendations.
server.py is ~838 lines — carrying over the prior recommendation to split into modules.
test_credentials: ada@coolpet.io / secret123 (legacy JWT). Tests use ephemeral signup accounts.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral signup users per test session + Google-session Mongo seeding (test-google-user-* / test_session_*). New tests create TEST_-prefixed pets which are deleted at test_delete_pet or via fixture ephemerality.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py now covers: (1) 15-digit IMEI persistence, (2) '860…' fallback generation, (3) instant WebSocket pet_update within ~1s of POST /pets, (4) history points within 2.5s. The only failing test is test_breach_exit_then_enter_events — it's a REAL regression, not a flaky test. Do NOT modify the test; fix the server-side race in _broadcast_initial_pet.
rca of the issue: test_breach_exit_then_enter_events failure RCA: POST /api/pets now schedules an async task _broadcast_initial_pet that (a) unconditionally writes inside_geofence=True at t≈0, then (b) every 400ms for 1.6s randomly drifts lat/lng, recomputes inside_geofence via _within_geofence(), and PERSISTS the result to db.pets. The breach test's fixture posts an 'inside' ingest packet immediately after pet creation to prime prev_inside=True. Because the background task keeps running, by the time the test's exit ingest packet arrives (~2s later — after fixture's inside_pkt), one of two races occurs: (i) the task's last drift frame lands with inside=False and is written AFTER the fixture's inside_pkt, so exit_pkt sees prev_inside=False and no 'exit' breach is recorded; or (ii) the task writes inside=True AFTER exit_pkt sets inside=False, so the subsequent in_pkt sees prev_inside=True and no 'enter' breach is recorded. Reproduction: pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py::test_breach_exit_then_enter_events (fails 3/3 runs). Mitigation: stop mutating db.pets.inside_geofence in _broadcast_initial_pet (either don't persist at all, or abort the loop once a real /iot/ingest has landed for the pet).
